title: External Integration Degradation and Fallback Policy
author: Maya Chen
content:
Overview
--------
This document defines Redwood Inference's standard policy and operator playbook for graceful degradation and fallback when external integrations (third-party APIs, partner services, and managed SaaS dependencies) impact user-facing inference workflows or platform control planes. The guidance balances user experience, cost containment, and operational safety while preserving security and compliance requirements.

Audience
--------
- Platform Operators and Oncall
- Service Owners that depend on third-party APIs (billing, embeddings, identity, telemetry vendors)
- Product & SRE teams planning integrations or runbooks

Scope
-----
Applies to all Redwood services that call external HTTP/gRPC APIs from the serving runtime, control plane, edge proxies, or background batch jobs. Exclusions: internal shared services (handled by internal service SLAs) and one-off ad-hoc scripts.

Goals and Constraints
---------------------
- Preserve core SLOs (latency, availability) for paid customer requests where possible.
- Avoid cascading failures from noisy 3rd-party dependencies.
- Prefer deterministic, testable fallbacks over ad-hoc behavior.
- Maintain auditability for regulatory-sensitive data flows; do not route restricted data to unapproved fallbacks.

Ownership
---------
- Policy owner: Platform Systems (eng-platform)
- Local implementer: Service owner for each product service that depends on an external integration
- Oncall escalation: Platform oncall -> Integration owner -> Partner ops (if SLA exists)

Degradation Tiers
-----------------
1) Tier 0 — Healthy: External integration operating within SLAs; normal behavior.
2) Tier 1 — Degraded: Intermittent errors or elevated latency (error rate > 2% OR p95 latency > 2x baseline). Automatic retries + soft-fallback (caching) enabled. Alert: P1? (see thresholds).
3) Tier 2 — Functional fallback: External integration unreliable (error rate > 5% or sustained latency). System switches to deterministic fallback behavior (cached responses, local model variant, reduced feature set). Alert: P1, page oncall.
4) Tier 3 — Protective shutdown: Integration causing cascading load or data risk. Circuit-breaker opens; writes are disabled and non-essential features blocked. Alert: P0, invoke incident playbook.

Fallback Matrix (example)
-------------------------
This table describes example fallback behaviours for common integration classes. Implementation MUST document the exact fallback no later than feature ship.

| Integration type | Normal action | Tier 1 fallback | Tier 2 fallback | Tier 3 protective action | Owner | Notes |
|---|---:|---|---|---|---|---|
| Billing API (partner) | Real-time quoted quota check | Retry w/ exponential backoff (3 attempts) | Use last-known quota (cache TTL 15m) and allow call with warning flag | Block write ops; degrade to read-only tenant mode | Billing-service | Ensure audit log for every write decision |
| Embeddings provider | Live embed call for similarity | Local LRU cache lookup (prefix match) | Serve with smaller-dimension local quantized model (approx) | Disable similarity-based features, fall back to title-only search | Vector-service | Must preserve PII filters before fallback |
| Identity provider (SSO) | Redirect to IdP | Use session cookie validation only (no refresh) | Local read-only token verification based on JWK cache | Reject new logins; route admin auth to emergency flow | Auth-service | Rollback safe-mode within 30m if traffic recovers |
| Telemetry ingest | Fire-and-forget POST | Buffer to local queue (disk-backed) | Drop low-priority telemetry; keep error/latency samples | Stop all telemetry; alert on monitor-only channel | Telemetry-agent | Ensure GDPR data residency preserved on buffer |

Operator Runbook (step-by-step)
-------------------------------
1) Detection
   - Monitor: integration-specific SLI (error rate, p95 latency, 50 ms alerts for high-frequency endpoints).
   - Alerting: page if SLI crosses Tier 2 thresholds for > 5 minutes.
2) Triage (platform oncall)
   - Verify alert in dashboards: call graph, external host latency, synthetic probes.
   - Check recent deploys and config changes via the deployment timeline.
   - If degraded, update the incident channel with the integration tier.
3) Mitigation
   - Engage automated controls: increase retry jitter, enable cached path, lower concurrency for integration client.
   - If Tier 2 requirements met, flip to documented fallback (feature flag + runtime switch). Use the pre-approved safe configuration only.
   - For Tier 3, open the circuit breaker and execute the protective shutdown script: 
     - run: scripts/integrations/open-circuit.sh --service=<service> --integration=<integration> --reason="cascading_load"
     - Post linked run command output to incident channel and set an audit tag.
4) Communication
   - Notify product and partner ops. Post templated status updates to the customer-facing status page for impacted tenants.
   - Document decisions taken in the incident channel and mark them for postmortem review.
5) Recovery
   - Close circuit only after partner has validated a fix AND the integration passes synthetic tests for 15 minutes.
   - Gradually ramp traffic using a canary (10% -> 50% -> 100%) while monitoring error budget consumption.
6) Post-incident
   - Capture timeline, decisions, metrics, and suggested runbook changes in a retrospective.

Implementation Checklist (pre-ship)
----------------------------------
- [ ] Integration design doc links to this policy.
- [ ] Explicit fallback behaviour documented in service README.
- [ ] Circuit breaker and rate limiter implemented in client library (see example below).
- [ ] Configurable fallbacks behind safe feature-flag controlled defaults.
- [ ] Synthetic probes and canary tests added to the platform synthetic test runner.
- [ ] Observability dashboards instrumented for SLI and fallback success rate.
- [ ] Security review complete for any data routed during fallback.

Example client config (YAML)
--------------------------
# Example: services/embedding-client/config.yaml
integration:
  host: https://api.partner-embeds.example
  timeout_ms: 1500
  max_retries: 3
  backoff_ms: 200
  circuit_breaker: true
  fallback_strategy: cached_then_local_model
  cache_ttl_seconds: 900
  allowed_data_classes_for_fallback: [non-sensitive, metadata]

Example client usage (pseudo-code)
----------------------------------
- try embed via partner API
- on 4xx/5xx or timeout: run exponential backoff up to max_retries
- on persistent failures: consult cache (prefix match)
- if cache miss and local-model policy enabled: call local quantized embedder
- if local-model unavailable: return graceful degraded response with metadata: {"fallback":"local_minimal","reason":"embedding provider error"}

Dashboards and Alerts (recommended set)
--------------------------------------
- Integration Overview panel: external latency p50/p95/p99, error rate, synthetic probe success rate
- Fallback activation metric: count of requests served by fallback path (per-minute)
- Circuit breaker state gauge: CLOSED/OPEN/HALF_OPEN
- Paging rules: page on Tier 2 sustained (5 minutes) or Tier 3 immediately

Alert thresholds (example)
------------------------
- p95 latency > 3x baseline for 5m -> WARNING (ticket)
- error rate > 2% for 10m -> PAGE (P2)
- error rate > 5% for 5m OR circuit open -> PAGE (P1)

Testing and Validation
----------------------
- Unit tests for client fallback logic (cache cold/hot, circuit transitions).
- Integration tests that simulate partner latency and errors; assert no customer-facing crash and correct telemetry emitted.
- Synthetic canary that injects partner failure and verifies controlled fallback during deployment.

Rollout guidance
----------------
- Feature-flag new fallback behind ops-only flag for 2 weeks of shadow traffic.
- Run a controlled exercise (gameday) quarterly to validate fallback paths and operator runbooks.

Security and Compliance Notes
-----------------------------
- Do not enable fallbacks that route regulated data to vendors or local models that do not meet the customer's data-residency/KMS requirements.
- Any cached or buffered data written to disk must be encrypted at rest and periodically scrubbed per retention policy.

Retrospective template (post-incident)
-------------------------------------
1) Summary (1–2 sentences)
2) Timeline with timestamps and actors
3) What went well (operator mitigation, quick rollback)
4) What failed (missing tests, bad defaults)
5) Action items with owners and due dates
6) Follow-ups: update tests, add new synthetic probes, refine thresholds

Appendix: Scripts and helper tools
----------------------------------
- scripts/integrations/open-circuit.sh — idempotent script to open integration circuit with audit tagging
- tools/fallback-sim — local simulator for validating fallback behaviour against noisy responses
- dashboards/third-party-integration-health.json — Grafana dashboard export (versioned)

Related documents
-----------------
- See the platform fallback catalog and the integration onboarding checklist for per-service requirements.
